doc_name: List of aviation accidents and incidents with a sole survivor
text: The earliest known aviation incident involving 10 or more people on board with a sole survivor occurred on 17 March 1929, when a New Jersey sightseeing flight crashed into a sand-filled freight car during an unsuccessful forced landing caused by engine failure. The pilot was thrown out upon impact and sustained serious injuries; the crash resulted in the deaths of all 13 individuals in the cabin and one additional person in the cockpit. The most recent aviation accident with a sole survivor is Air India Flight 171, which crashed on 12 June 2025 and holds the record for the highest number of fatalities among any sole survivor crash. A table lists known aviation accidents and incidents with a sole survivor that meet specific criteria: "Nationality" indicates the country of the sole survivor, and "Age" refers to the sole survivor's age at the time of the event. In some cases, details about the sole survivor are unknown or not disclosed.
